failure_patterns.pattern: rule_ignored: Answers missed the requested relation or overlooked clue constraints, choosing a related entity or an unsupported candidate despite better contextual evidence.

rejected_edits.content: For personal names, use the conventional identifying form supported by the clue and context, not automatically the fullest form found in a source. Include the given and family names needed to identify the person, but omit middle initials, honorifics, and generational suffixes unless requested or needed to distinguish people. When a clue supplies part of a name and asks for completion, give only the missing component.
rejected_edits.target: Use a full canonical personal name when the clue does not supply a name component; when it supplies part of a name and asks for completion, give only the missing component.

rejected_edits.content: - For a prompt consisting only of a work title and year, do not default to a broad category such as genre. Use the context to identify the salient named relation associated with the work (for example, its director or author) and answer with that entity; give a category only when the prompt asks for classification.

### Distinguishing formal entity names
When direct evidence distinguishes related political entities or governments by their formal names, preserve the distinguishing words in the answer rather than shortening the name to a potentially ambiguous common label.
